title: Thiamine Biosynthesis Genes and Chemicals
summary: This cluster consists of genes and proteins involved in thiamine biosynthesis, along with the chemical thiamine itself. The genes include THI5, THI21, THI72, BAT2, GCV1, GCV2, GCV3, SNO2, and SNZ2, which are likely involved in the production or regulation of thiamine. HMP is also present, possibly as a precursor or intermediate in the biosynthesis pathway. The relationship between these entities is likely metabolic, with the genes and proteins contributing to the production of thiamine.
